mainTopic: What counts as 'selling' a stolen animal, when a theft is complete (lifting, taking out, or pulling), and whether חכמים required משיכה for שומרים.
overview: The ברייתא ends by listing ways of passing on a stolen animal that count as 'selling' it, such as giving it to הקדש, trading it, or giving it as a gift. In each of these cases the thief pays four or five times. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא teaches two new points. First, here יש שליח לדבר עבירה, because the פסוק joins slaughtering with selling, and selling always involves another person. Second, giving the animal to הקדש counts as a sale. A new משנה then teaches that the fine applies only if the theft was completed: lifting the animal, or getting it out of the owner's property, completes it, but pulling it inside the property does not. The same rule applies when the thief hands the animal to a creditor or a שומר who moves it. אמימר asks whether חכמים required משיכה for שומרים. After a back-and-forth with רב יימר and רב אשי, the גמרא proves from the משנה that they did, and backs this up with רבי אלעזר and a ברייתא. The amud ends as the גמרא begins asking what kind of rental that ברייתא means.

steps.title: List of transfers that count as selling a stolen animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists seven ways of passing on a stolen animal. In every one, the thief pays four or five times.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole and consecrated it, stole and sold it on credit, stole and traded it, stole and gave it as a gift, stole and paid his debt with it, stole and paid off something he bought on credit, or stole and sent it as engagement gifts to his father-in-law's house, he pays four or five times.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list. It names many ways of passing a stolen animal to someone else, and each one counts like selling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה makes a thief pay four or five times only if he slaughters or sells the animal. This list stretches 'selling' to cover any transfer of ownership, even with no cash, such as a gift, a trade, paying a debt, or giving it to הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it, giving it to the בית המקדש
He sold it on credit, with payment to come later
He traded it for something else
Gifts a groom sends to his engaged bride
Paying four times (sheep) or five times (ox) the value

phrases.english: If he stole and consecrated it;
stole and sold it on credit;
stole and exchanged it;
stole and gave it as a gift;
stole and repaid his debt with it;
stole and paid with it for what he bought on credit;
stole and sent it as gifts to his father-in-law's house –
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any transfer of the stolen animal's ownership counts as 'selling' and brings תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the ברייתא adds, since its rulings seem obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is coming to teach. This sets up the next steps, which find the new point in its first part and its last part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes a ברייתא should not state the obvious. Plainly, giving a stolen animal away is like selling it, so the גמרא looks for a hidden new point.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (What is the new point?)

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the ברייתא teaches, beyond obvious points.

steps.title: The first part teaches that agency works here for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The first part of the ברייתא teaches that if a thief has someone else slaughter the animal, the thief is liable. Here יש שליח לדבר עבירה, even though that is not the rule anywhere else in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part teaches us, with the case of 'he stole and gave it to another, who slaughtered it', that there is agency for a sin. Even though in the whole תורה there is no agency for a sin, here there is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first part of the ברייתא has a real new point. A thief is responsible when his שליח slaughters the animal for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if you send someone to do a sin, the sin counts as the agent's own act, not yours. This is called אין שליח לדבר עבירה. Here the תורה makes an exception, so the thief pays four or five times even though someone else did the slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a ברייתא or משנה
An agent sent to do a sin
The rule that a sender is not responsible for a sin his agent does

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this cancels the general rule of אין שליח לדבר עבירה. That rule still holds everywhere else. Theft followed by slaughter is a special exception.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous exception to a basic rule of agency in the תורה.

phrases.english: The first clause teaches us,
through 'he stole and gave it to another, and he slaughtered it' –
that there is agency for a transgression.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּבְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ
phrases.english: Even though in the entire Torah
there is no agency for a transgression,
here there is agency for a transgression.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 for the first part of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first part teaches that here יש שליח לדבר עבירה: the thief is liable for slaughter done by his agent.

steps.title: Why is this case an exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why agency works for a sin here when it does not work anywhere else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of this exception. This sets up the proof from the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exception to a rule that applies across the whole תורה needs a clear source. The גמרא wants to know what tells us this case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the exception stated in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for saying יש שליח לדבר עבירה in the case of slaughtering a stolen animal.

steps.title: Slaughtering is compared to selling
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts 'slaughters it' next to 'sells it'. Selling always needs another person, so slaughtering done through another person also makes the thief liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And slaughters it or sells it.' Just as selling cannot happen without another person, so too slaughtering through another person makes him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. Because the פסוק joins slaughtering with selling, the two work the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale needs a buyer, so the תורה must mean a thief is liable for a sale that involves someone else. Since slaughtering is placed right next to selling, it is treated the same way. A thief is liable even when another person does the slaughtering for him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And slaughters it or sells it' (the פסוק about the thief)
Through another person
He becomes liable

steps.whatToRemember: The exception comes from the פסוק itself. Slaughtering is learned from selling, and selling always involves another person.

phrases.english: "And slaughters it" and "sells it";
just as selling –

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר דְּלָאו עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר,
phrases.english: which is impossible except through another person,

phrases.aramaic: אַף טְבִיחָה עַל יְדֵי אַחֵר – מִחַיַּיב.
phrases.english: so too for slaughtering through another person – he is liable.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Slaughtering is placed next to selling in the פסוק. Since selling always involves another person, slaughtering done through another also makes the thief liable.

steps.title: The last part teaches that הקדש counts as a sale
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the ברייתא teaches that giving the stolen animal to הקדש counts as selling it. Selling to a person and 'selling to Heaven' are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the last part teaches us 'he stole and consecrated it': what difference does it make to me if he sold it to an ordinary person, and what difference if he sold it to Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to 'what is it teaching us?'. The new point is that הקדש counts as a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a sale needs a human buyer, so הקדש would not count. The גמרא says ownership moved away from the thief either way. Whether it went to a person or to the בית המקדש makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a ברייתא or משנה
What difference does it make to me (the two are the same)
An ordinary person (not הקדש)
To Heaven, meaning to הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has two new points. In the first part, יש שליח לדבר עבירה for slaughtering. In the last part, giving the animal to הקדש counts as a sale.

phrases.english: And the latter clause teaches us
'he stole and consecrated' –
what difference is it to me if he sold it to an ordinary person,
and what difference if he sold it to Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of step 2 and answers it for the last part of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The last part teaches that הקדש counts as a sale, because a transfer to Heaven is like a transfer to a person.

steps.title: Where the theft and slaughter happen decides the fine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases of stealing, slaughtering and selling inside or outside the owner's property. If any stage happened outside, the thief pays ארבעה וחמשה. If everything happened inside the owner's property, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone stole an animal in the owner's property and slaughtered or sold it outside, or stole it outside and slaughtered or sold it inside, or did everything outside, he pays four or five times. But if he stole, slaughtered and sold it all inside the owner's property, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives four cases and explains that only when everything happens inside the owner's property is the thief exempt from ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine of ארבעה וחמשה needs a finished theft first, and a theft is not finished while the animal is still in רשות הבעלים. Once the animal has left the owner's property at any point, the theft is complete. After that, slaughtering or selling it brings the fine. If it never left, there was no finished theft, so slaughtering or selling it does not trigger the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. This marks the start of a new משנה
the owner's property or domain
slaughtered or sold
the fine of paying four times (sheep) or five times (ox) for a stolen animal that was slaughtered or sold
exempt

steps.confusionAlert: In the case of 'stole outside, slaughtered inside,' he is still liable. Once the theft was completed outside, bringing the animal back in does not undo it.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If he stole in the owner's domain,
and slaughtered or sold it outside their domain;
or if he stole outside their domain,
and slaughtered or sold it in their domain;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁגָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר חוּץ מֵרְשׁוּתָם –
phrases.english: or if he stole, slaughtered or sold, all outside their domain,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גָּנַב וְטָבַח וּמָכַר בִּרְשׁוּתָם – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: But if he stole, slaughtered or sold, all in their domain, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of the ברייתא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארבעה וחמשה applies only if the theft was completed, meaning the animal left רשות הבעלים at some stage. If everything stayed inside, the thief is exempt.

steps.title: The animal dies while being pulled out
steps.stepSummary: If the thief was pulling the animal out and it died before leaving the owner's property, he is פטור. If he lifted it, or got it out, and then it died, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was leading it out and it died while still in the owner's property, he is exempt. If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's property and then it died, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks exactly when the theft becomes complete, using the case of an animal that died during the theft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling an animal does not complete the theft while it is still on the owner's property, so its death there leaves the thief exempt. Lifting it completes the theft even inside the owner's property. Getting it out of the property also completes the theft. Once the theft is complete, the thief carries responsibility for it, even if it dies afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: pulling or leading it along
he lifted it up
he took it out
liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the moment when the theft becomes complete, which is the basis for the next case and for the גמרא's question.

phrases.english: If he was leading it and going out,
and it died in the owner's domain, he is exempt.
If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's domain,
and it died, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by defining the exact moment the theft is completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling inside רשות הבעלים does not complete the theft. Lifting the animal, or taking it out, does.

steps.title: The thief hands the stolen animal to someone else
steps.stepSummary: The thief gives the animal to a כהן for his firstborn son, to a creditor, or to various kinds of שומרים. The same rule applies: if it died while that person was pulling it inside the owner's property, the thief is פטור. If that person lifted it or took it out, the thief is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave it for his firstborn son's redemption, or to a creditor, an unpaid watchman, a borrower, a paid watchman or a renter, and that person was pulling it and it died in the owner's property, the thief is exempt. If that person lifted it or took it out of the owner's property and then it died, the thief is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same rule to a case where someone else moves the animal for the thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the thief does not move the animal himself. He gives it to another person, and that person moves it. The משנה treats that person's act as if the thief did it. So the same line applies: pulling inside the owner's property leaves the thief exempt, while lifting or taking it out makes him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: the redemption of his firstborn son (פדיון הבן)
a creditor
an unpaid watchman
a borrower
a paid watchman
a renter

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the thief moves the animal himself or someone moves it for him, the theft is complete only through lifting it or getting it out of רשות הבעלים.

phrases.english: If he gave it for his firstborn son,
phrases.notes: He means using the stolen animal as payment to the כהן for redeeming his firstborn.

phrases.english: or to a creditor, to an unpaid watchman,
to a borrower, to a paid watchman, or to a renter;
and he was pulling it,
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the person who received the animal, not the thief.

phrases.english: and it died in the owner's domain, the thief is exempt.
If he lifted it or took it out of the owner's domain,
and it died, the thief is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 8 to a case where another person moves the animal for the thief.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the recipient pulls the animal and it dies inside רשות הבעלים, the thief is exempt. When the recipient lifts it or takes it out, the thief is liable.

steps.title: אמימר asks whether a watchman's responsibility needs pulling
steps.stepSummary: אמימר asks whether חכמים required משיכה for שומרים. In other words, does a watchman become responsible only after he pulls the item?
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר asked: Did the חכמים institute pulling for watchmen, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with אמימר's question, which grows out of the משנה's mention of שומרים. The גמרא is setting up a discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, the deal is not binding until the buyer does an act of acquisition, such as משיכה. אמימר asks whether חכמים made the same rule for a שומר. If they did, his responsibility starts only once he pulls the animal. If not, it starts as soon as he agrees to watch it.

keyTerms.meaning: short for גְּמָרָא. This marks where the גמרא's discussion begins
he asks or raises a question
they (חכמים) instituted, made a rule
pulling, a way of acquiring an animal or object
watchmen, people who take responsibility for someone else's property

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ameimar asks:
Did they institute pulling for watchmen, or not?
phrases.notes: 'They' means חכמים. The question is whether a watchman's responsibility starts only after he pulls the item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's list of שומרים by asking when a שומר's responsibility begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חכמים required משיכה before a שומר becomes responsible, as they did for a buyer in a sale.

steps.title: רב יימר brings a proof from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר quotes the משנה about giving the stolen animal to a כהן, a creditor, or a שומר. It says that if the animal died while 'he' was pulling it inside the owner's property, the thief is פטור. רב יימר argues that 'he' means the שומר, which shows that חכמים required משיכה for שומרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: Come and hear. If the thief gave the animal for his son's פדיון הבן, or to his creditor, or to an unpaid watchman, a borrower, a paid watchman, or a renter, and that person was pulling it out and it died in the owner's property, the thief is פטור. Isn't this talking about the watchman pulling it? So we learn that חכמים required pulling for watchmen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר answers אמימר's question by quoting the משנה from step 9. He reads it as proof that a שומר is not responsible until he pulls the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שומר became responsible as soon as he agreed to watch the animal, the animal would already count as taken from the owner when the thief handed it over, before any pulling. The thief would then be liable for the theft. Since the משנה says the thief is פטור when the animal dies while still being pulled inside the owner's property, the שומר's taking only counts through משיכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling: a way of taking possession or responsibility
Unpaid watchman
Paid watchman
Learn from this: drawing a conclusion

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said: Come and hear:
If the thief gave it for redeeming his firstborn son
or to his creditor,
to an unpaid watchman or to a borrower,
to a paid watchman or to a renter;
and he was pulling it and going out,
and it died in the owner's property, the thief is exempt.
What, is it not the watchman who was pulling?
So learn from it that they required pulling for watchmen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer אמימר's question from step 10 using the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים required משיכה before a שומר becomes responsible.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: if the animal died while being pulled out inside the owner's property, the thief is פטור.

steps.title: Maybe the one pulling was a thief
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed back: the person pulling the animal in that line of the משנה might be a thief, not the שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No, it is talking about a thief.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר rejects רב יימר's reading of the משנה. He says the one pulling the animal could be a thief who was stealing it from the creditor or the שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a thief was the one pulling, the line tells us nothing about when a שומר becomes responsible. It would only repeat that a thief is פטור until the animal leaves the property. So the proof about משיכה for שומרים falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Thief

phrases.english: He said to him: No, it is talking about a thief.
phrases.notes: אמימר is speaking. He means the animal was already with the שומר, and a thief was pulling it out of there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 11 by reading the משנה differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the reading of the משנה, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the שומר is the one pulling, but it could be a thief.

steps.title: But the beginning of the משנה already taught this
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר objects: the first part of the משנה already taught that a thief who dies pulling inside the property is פטור. Why would it say it again?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה already taught this in the first part!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר challenges אמימר's new reading. If this line is about a thief, it just repeats the start of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first part (step 8) already said that a thief who was pulling the animal and it died in the owner's property is פטור. A משנה does not usually repeat itself for no reason. So reading this line as being about a thief makes it extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
It taught

phrases.english: But it already taught this in the first part!
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to the line from step 8 about the thief pulling the animal.

steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's reading that the one pulling is a thief.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the line a repeat of the first part of the משנה.

steps.title: Two cases: stealing from the owner and from a שומר
steps.stepSummary: אמימר answers that the משנה could teach the rule twice: once for a thief stealing from the owner's house, and again for a thief stealing from a שומר's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught a thief who stole from the owner's house, and it taught a thief who stole from a watchman's house.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defends his reading. The repeat is not wasted, because each line covers a different place the animal was stolen from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה is about stealing from the owner. The later line, in אמימר's reading, is about stealing from the creditor or שומר who was holding the animal. So it adds a new case and is not a pure repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner's house
The watchman's house

phrases.english: It taught a thief who stole from the owner's house,
and it taught a thief who stole from a watchman's house.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two lines into two different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later line seemed to repeat the first part word for word in meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: One line is about stealing from the owner, the other about stealing from a שומר.

steps.title: רב אשי: there is no difference, so the proof stands
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells אמימר not to push away רב יימר's proof this way. Stealing from a שומר and stealing from the owner are the same, so the משנה would not teach both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: Do not reject the proof. What difference is there to me between a thief who stole from a watchman's house and a thief who stole from the owner's house?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects אמימר's answer from step 14. This brings back רב יימר's proof that a שומר needs משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law for a thief is the same no matter whose house he took the animal from. So the משנה would have no reason to teach both cases. That means the later line must be about the שומר pulling, just as רב יימר said.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not push it away: do not reject the proof
What difference is it to me: the two cases are the same

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי restores רב יימר's proof: the משנה shows that חכמים required משיכה for שומרים, since the 'thief' reading would make the משנה repeat a case with no real difference.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תְּדַחֲיֵיהּ;
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him: Do not reject it;
phrases.notes: He is telling אמימר not to push away רב יימר's proof.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי גַּנָּב שֶׁגָּנַב מִבֵּית שׁוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: what difference is it to me if a thief stole from a watchman's house,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי גַּנָּב שֶׁגָּנַב מִבֵּית בְּעָלִים?
phrases.english: or if a thief stole from the owner's house?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תְּדַחֲיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer in step 14, which brings back the proof of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אמימר's answer that the משנה teaches two separate thief cases.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no legal difference between stealing from a שומר and stealing from the owner, so the משנה would not teach both.

steps.title: The proof stands: the one pulling is the שומר
steps.stepSummary: Since the other reading was rejected, the 'he' in the משנה must be the שומר, so חכמים required משיכה for שומרים. The גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it the שומר? So learn from this that חכמים set up pulling for שומרים. Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב יימר's proof and accepts it. The person pulling the animal in the משנה is the שומר, so חכמים required משיכה for שומרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רב אשי showed that reading the line as being about a thief makes the משנה repeat itself for no reason. With that reading gone, only the שומר reading is left. So רב יימר's proof from step 11 works, and the גמרא says 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it... (the only reading left)
Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer: חכמים required משיכה for a שומר, just as for a buyer.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it the bailee?
phrases.notes: He means the 'he' pulling the animal in the משנה is the שומר, not a thief.

phrases.english: And learn from this that they instituted pulling for bailees?
Yes, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the rival reading rejected in step 15, רב יימר's proof from step 11 is restored and accepted.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי אלעזר said this clearly: just as חכמים required משיכה for buyers, they required it for שומרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said: רבי אלעזר says: just as they set up pulling for buyers, they set up pulling for שומרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an אמורא who said the same ruling outright. This backs up the conclusion just reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was first learned only by reading the משנה closely. Now we see that רבי אלעזר stated it openly. He links שומרים to לקוחות: the same act that finishes a sale also starts a שומר's responsibility.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (by an אמורא)
Just as... so too
Buyers
People who guard someone else's things

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Elazar says:
Just as they instituted pulling for purchasers,
so too they instituted pulling for bailees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an אמורא's open statement supporting the conclusion of step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That חכמים required משיכה for שומרים

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches it too, and adds a rule about renting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule about משיכה for שומרים. It adds that just as land is acquired with money, a document, or חזקה, so is שכירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: just as they set up pulling for buyers, they set up pulling for שומרים. And just as land is acquired with money, a document, or חזקה, so a rental is acquired with money, a document, or חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that teaches the same rule. This gives the conclusion even stronger support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is an older source from the time of the תנאים, so this is stronger support than an אמורא alone. The ברייתא also adds a new rule: a rental deal is made the same three ways land is bought. That new rule leads to the question in the next step.

steps.raayaObject: That חכמים required משיכה for שומרים

steps.title: What kind of rental does the ברייתא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of rental the ברייתא is talking about and starts to suggest an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rental of what? If you say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of rented property the ברייתא means. It is setting up its next move, a first suggestion that starts with 'אילימא'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said only 'a rental' without saying of what. The word 'אילימא' tells us the גמרא will suggest one answer and probably find a problem with it. The rest of the question continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Of what?
If you say (a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
